IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r2.claim: The lowly are the weak, chronically ill, children, and those unable to find a way or means; sāfil is formed like ʿāl from the verbs safala and ʿalā.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r2.anchor: والسافلون: هم الضعفاء والزمنى الأطفال، ومن لا يستطيع حيلة، ولا يجد سبيلا.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r3.claim: The verse resembles the return to decrepit age: old people become confused and unsteady, weakened in body, sight, hearing, and ability to act righteously.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r3.anchor: ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر [النحل: 70]

DAMGHANI:v1p237/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p237/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p237/r10.claim: Asfal sāfilīn means decrepit old age, after which a person’s deeds are no longer recorded.

BURSEVI:v10p360/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360/r7.claim: Those who fail to live by their God-given attributes are made among the people of the Fire, lower than the state they could have attained; inward corruption produces outward degradation.
BURSEVI:v10p360/r7.anchor: لعدم جريانه على موجب ما خلقناه عليه من الصفات التي لو عمل بمقتضاها لكان في أعلى عليين

BURSEVI:v10p360/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360/r8.claim: “Lowest of the low” can describe the object in its fallen state or a deleted place that is the lowest of places; the first grammatical analysis is clearer, and the descent applies to some people immersed in animal desires and bodily, satanic, and predatory darkness.
BURSEVI:v10p360/r8.anchor: وأسفل سافلين إما حال من المفعول أي رددناه حال كونه أسفل سافلين أو صفة لمكان محذوف

BURSEVI:v10p360/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360/r9.claim: In the inward reading, the relevant measure is the inner form rather than outward appearance.
BURSEVI:v10p360/r9.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الاعتبار إنما هو بالصورة الباطنة لا بالصورة الظاهرة

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r1.speaker: سعدي
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r1.claim: Sa‘di's verse says true stature is uprightness of heart, not bodily height; even a visually handsome unbeliever can be inwardly ugly.
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r1.anchor: ره راست بايدنه بالاي راست كه كافرهم ازروى صورت وماست

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r2.claim: At resurrection, inner traits appear in outward forms, so people emerge in groups and their forms vary according to their qualities.
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r2.anchor: فإن صفاتهم الباطنة تظهر على صورهم الظاهرة فتتنوع صورهم بحسب صفاتهم

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r3.claim: An alternative takes the descent as decrepit old age after youth and weakness after strength, with the back bending, hair whitening, and hearing and sight failing.
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r3.anchor: وقيل رددناه إلى أرذل العمر وهو الهرم بعد الشباب والضعف بعد القوة

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r4.claim: A Persian poem evokes the old person's formerly strong body and dark curls, now reduced to weakness and needing a shroud.

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r5.speaker: عين المعاني
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r5.claim: Ayn al-Ma‘ani notes that Ibn Mas‘ud's codex lacks the generic article before “lowest,” because the phrase refers specifically to the lowest decrepit state rather than all disabled people.
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r5.anchor: ولم تدخل لام الجنس في سافلين كما ورد في مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r6.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r6.claim: Kashf al-Asrar identifies the lowly as the frail: the sick, chronically ill, and children; the very old are lower still.
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r6.anchor: وفي كشف الأسرار السافلون هم الضعفاء من المرضى والزمني والأطفال

QASHANI:95:4-5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:95:4-5/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:95:4-5/r2.claim: People descend to the lowest rank by becoming veiled in darkness, adopting vicious traits, and turning from virtue; they become inmates of nature’s prison and fire.
QASHANI:95:4-5/r2.anchor: لاحتجابه بالظلمة عن النور والوقوف مع رذائل الأخلاق والإعراض عن الفضائل

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.claim: The oaths validate the premise that God created humans in the finest form: those who honor innate guidance, accept the messengers, believe, and do right earn eternal reward, while those who reject it fall into ruin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.anchor: These verses mention the premise which is validated by the oaths sworn in the previous verses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r3.claim: The verse states a divine law: free will determines whether a person honors the best creation or lapses into lowliness, which God then deepens into humiliation and Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r3.anchor: it depends upon his own attitude whether he remains the best of God’s creation or reverts to a lowly state

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r4.claim: Syntactically, asfala is an adverb of place and sāfilīn is a circumstantial accusative tied to the object pronoun, indicating God casts a person down because that person inclines to disgrace.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r5.claim: Although sāfilīn is plural while the pronoun is singular, al-insān denotes a human kind and is effectively plural, so the Qur’an uses both singular and plural pronouns for it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r5.anchor: both singular and plural pronouns are used

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r3.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r3.claim: Farāhī identifies the Mount of Figs with Jūdī and presents Adam’s and Noah’s episodes there as examples of divine retribution.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r3.anchor: Im ām Far āhī writes: The Mounts of Figs is the first place in which the first instance of worldly retribution

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r4.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r4.claim: Farāhī recounts that Adam and his wife forgot their covenant, ate the forbidden fruit after Satan’s temptation, and lost their success and heavenly clothing; the Qur’an recalls the episode.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r4.anchor: Im ām Far āhī writes: The Mounts of Figs is the first place

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r5.claim: The account notes that the Torah identifies the leaves Adam and Eve used to cover themselves as fig leaves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r5.anchor: it is mentioned in the Torah that once Adam and Eve were divested of their apparel

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r6.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r6.claim: After Adam and Eve repented and God accepted them, He promised guidance and reward to its followers, making this a second covenant with Adam.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r6.anchor: the Almighty accepted their repentance and promised to reveal guidance to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r1.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r1.claim: The Adam episode has two sides: God removed one favor because of the broken promise, then gave another after Adam and Eve recognized their folly and repented.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r1.anchor: the Almighty deprived Adam of one of His favours and blessed him with another great favour

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r2.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r2.claim: At Noah’s time God destroyed wrongdoers near the mountain and saved the righteous from the Flood, as shown in the Jūdī landing and Noah’s later promise of peace and blessings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r2.anchor: Im ām Far āhī has explained it thus: In his times, the Almighty destroyed the wrongdoers near this mountain

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r3.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r3.claim: Farāhī concludes that the Mount of Figs is a major site where God’s law of retribution became manifest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r3.anchor: the law of retribution of the Almighty manifested itself.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r4.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r4.claim: Farāhī says that in Jesus’ final years God transferred the sharī‘ah and trust from the Jews to Abraham’s other line; Jesus grieved for his people as they pursued his life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p375/r4.anchor: It was on this mountain that the Almighty took away His shar īah from the Jews and gave it to the other branch

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p376/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p376/r1.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p376/r1.claim: Farāhī cites Jesus’ rejected-stone saying and his warning that God’s kingdom would be taken from the Jews and given to a fruitful people as evidence of their lost trust.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p376/r1.anchor: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures, ‘The stone that the builders rejected

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r1.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r1.claim: At Sinai God aided an oppressed people for their patience, freed Israel from Pharaoh, and gave them a law that punished its enemies; this illustrates favor to the oppressed and punishment of wrongdoers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r3.claim: Abraham’s faithfulness brought leadership after his greater sacrifice; God extended the promise only to descendants who follow him, excluding those who wrong themselves through disbelief or idolatry.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r3.anchor: this promise of His does not relate to people

QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r11.claim: One interpretation of being returned to the lowest state is reaching decrepit old age, senility, and infirmity.
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r11.anchor: إلى أراذل العمر وهو حال الخرف والهرم

QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r12.claim: Another interpretation is being returned to Hell and the abyss in the ugliest form; on this reading, the opening is general and the ending refers specifically to disbelievers.
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r12.anchor: إلى النار والهاوية في أقبح صورة ؛ فيكون أول الآية عاما

QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r13.claim: The old-age interpretation applies only to some people, since not everyone reaches senility.
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r13.anchor: إذ ليس كل الناس يبلغون حال الهرم

QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r15.claim: Another interpretation is that being returned to the lowest state means a state of misery and disbelief, from which believers are excepted.
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r15.anchor: إلى حال الشقاوة والكفر إلا المؤمنين

TUSTARI:95:5/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:95:5/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:95:5/r1.claim: Being returned to the lowest state means passing from one condition to another until old age.
TUSTARI:95:5/r1.anchor: يعني نقلناه من حال إلى حال حتى أدركه الهرم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r2.claim: The surah is Meccan for most commentators; Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatada say Madinan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r2.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول الجمهور. وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: مدنية.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r3.claim: After praising the Prophet's perfected creation and character, the surah describes the one who opposes him being brought low in this world and the next; mankind was created ready to accept truth but may be moved to a base state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r3.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها من كمله الله خلقا وخلقا وفضله على سائر العالم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r9.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك والنخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r9.claim: ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and al-Nakhaʿī take the descent to the lowest state as senility, loss of reason, and failing cognition; the exception is disconnected because a believing elder's pen is lifted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r9.anchor: ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين، قال عكرمة والضحاك والنخعي: بالهرم وذهول العقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r10.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو العالية وابن زيد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Ibn Zayd, and Qatada say the lowest state is Hell for disbelief, making the exception connected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد وأبو العالية وابن زيد وقتادة أيضا:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r11.claim: The majority read sāfilīn indefinite; ʿAbd Allāh reads it definite with the article.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: سافلين منكرا وعبد الله: السافلين معرفا بالألف واللام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī embellishes both readings as physical degradation in Hell or the bodily reversal of old age after an upright, handsome creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r12.anchor: وأخذ الزمخشري أقوال السلف وحسنها ببلاغته وانتقاء ألفاظه فقال: في أحسن تعديل لشكله وصورته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r13.claim: The author calls al-Zamakhsharī's elaboration excessive and begins to explain the continued reward of righteous people who reach old age.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r13.anchor: انتهى، وفيه تكثير. وعلى أن ذلك الرد هو إلى الهرم، فالمعنى:

FARRA:v3p276/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p276/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p276/r6.claim: The best human form is bodily balance and the vigor of youth; God then returns many people to decrepit old age, though the wording is singular and distributive.
FARRA:v3p276/r6.anchor: يقول: إنا لنبلغ بالآدمي أحسن تقويمه، وهو اعتداله واستواء شبابه، وهو أحسن ما يكون، ثم نرده بعد ذلك إلى أرذل العمر،

FARRA:v3p276/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p276/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p276/r8.claim: Asfal sāfilīn means the Fire, with believers excepted; the generic singular “human” can refer to a group, as believers are excepted from loss.
FARRA:v3p276/r8.anchor: ويقال: «ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين» (5) . إلى النار ثم استثنى فقال: «إلا الذين آمنوا» استثناء من الإنسان: لأن معنى الإنسان:

FARRA:v3p276/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p276/r9.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v3p276/r9.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading is asfal al-sāfilīn; the singular asfal sāfil would also be grammatical, but the plural fits generic humanity.
FARRA:v3p276/r9.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله «أسفل السافلين » ، ولو كانت: أسفل سافل لكان صوابا لأن لفظ الإنسان. واحد،

FARRA:v3p277/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p277/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p277/r1.claim: A singular subject can resume as plural when generic, and a plural can resume as singular; he illustrates this with Qur'anic usage.
FARRA:v3p277/r1.anchor: فإذا كان الواحد غير مقصود له رجع اسمه بالتوحيد وبالجمع

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r2.claim: One interpretation takes asfal sāfilīn as decrepit old age, with children, chronically ill people, and the aged at its lowest stage.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r2.anchor: 5، 6- {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} إلى الهرم، و "السافلون" هم: الأطفال والزمنى والهرمى.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan instead interprets asfal sāfilīn as the Fire.

MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r3.claim: Asfal sāfilīn means the most decrepit age, with a person's condition changing from stage to stage.
MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r3.anchor: «أسفل سافلين» (5) أي أرذل العمر وبدل حالا بعد حال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r1.claim: Thumma indicates temporal or rank succession; radd may mean making someone among the lowest, with أسفل as its second object.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r1.anchor: للتراخي الزماني أو الرتبي والرد إما بمعنى الجعل فينصب مفعولين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r2.claim: On this reading, God makes the person among Hell's inhabitants, lowest in form and constitution for failing to live by the original qualities.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى ثم جعلناه من أهل النار الذين هم أقبح من كل قبيح وأسفل من كل سافل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, radd means changing a state, with أسفل as a circumstantial description of the person made ugliest and most deformed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد بالرد تغيير الحال فهو متعد لواحدة وأسفل حال من المفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r4.claim: A further parse takes radd in its basic sense, with an omitted preposition: returned to the lowest place, Hell or its lowest depth.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r4.anchor: وأن يكون الرد بمعناه المعروف وأسفل منصوب بنزع الخافض

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r5.claim: The plural rational form السافلين is awkward for places; a proposed alternative is the lowest level among those in the levels of Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r5.anchor: ويعكر على هذا جمعها جمع العقلاء وكونه للفاصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r6.speaker: عكرمة، الضحاك، النخعي، قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r6.claim: They explain the return as old age and weakness of visible and inner faculties, reversing youth's straight posture, dark hair, keen senses, strength, and wit.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة والضحاك والنخعي وقتادة في رواية المراد بذلك رده إلى الهرم وضعف القوى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r7.claim: The old-age reading applies to the human species, so it does not imply that every individual undergoes senility.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r7.anchor: وهو باعتبار الجنس فلا يلزم أن يكون كل الإنسان كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r8.speaker: الحسن، مجاهد، أبو العالية، ابن زيد، قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r8.claim: They give the apparent contextual reading: the unbeliever is made hideous on Judgment Day after having been created in a beautiful form.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r8.anchor: والظاهر ما لاءم ذلك كما هو المروي عن الحسن ومجاهد وأبي العالية وابن زيد وقتادة أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r9.claim: The author finds the Judgment-Day reading more consistent with context; the old-age interpretation is contrary to the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r9.anchor: ومن هنا قيل إنه خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r10.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r10.claim: He reads السالفين with the definite article.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله السالفين مقرونا بأل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r2.claim: The first interpretation is return to old age: intellect diminishes and the body weakens; the elderly are lower in condition than the weak, chronically ill, and children.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r2.anchor: يريد إلى الهرم وأرذل العمر، فينقص عقله ويضعف بدنه، والسافلون: هم الضعفاء والزمنى والأطفال،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r3.claim: The phrase asfal safilin is indefinite to encompass the whole category, as in calling someone the most generous of those standing rather than of the known group.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r3.anchor: نكرة تعم الجنس، كما تقول: فلان أكرم قائم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r4.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r4.claim: Abdullah's codex reads the phrase with the definite form, asfal al-safilin.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r5.claim: They offer another interpretation: the return is to Hell, whose levels descend one below another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن، وقتادة، ومجاهد: يعني ثم رددناه إلى النار، يعني إلى أسفل السافلين،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the return is to Hell in the worst form, as a pig.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r6.anchor: قال أبو العالية: يعني إلى النار في شر صورة، في صورة خنزير.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r7.claim: Under the old-age interpretation, faculties and deeds cease, but believers who practiced righteousness keep receiving the record of deeds they used to perform after becoming feeble.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r7.anchor: فزالت عقولهم وانقطعت أعمالهم، فلا يكتب لهم حسنة إلا الذين آمنوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that some people reached decrepit old age in the Prophet's time; the verse excused them and promised their earlier reward after their faculties were lost.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم نفر ردوا إلى أرذل العمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأنزل الله تعالى عذرهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r9.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r9.claim: Ikrima says old age does not harm a person whom God seals upon the best deeds he practiced.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r9.anchor: قال عكرمة: لم يضر هذا الشيخ [كبره]

BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r3.claim: God returned humans to the lowest level by making them inhabitants of Hell or to Hell itself; alternatively, this means decrepit old age.
BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r3.anchor: { ثم رددنه أسفل سفلين } بأن جعلناه من أهل النار أو إلى أسفل سافلين وهو النار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468/r3.claim: Linked to al-Sharḥ, the surah presents humanity and especially the Prophet as the finest created kind, Abraham as its noblest root, and Mecca as its best land; God raises or lowers whom He wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468/r3.anchor: خصه بأن جعل نوعه صلى الله عليه وسلم أكمل الأنواع وهو الإنسان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#s095/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#s095/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#s095/r3.claim: The surah continues al-Sharḥ by presenting the Prophet’s kind as creation’s finest, Abraham as its noblest root, Mecca as the best land, and God as the one who raises or lowers whom He wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#s095/r3.anchor: خصه بأن جعل نوعه صلى الله عليه وسلم أكمل الأنواع وهو الإنسان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r5.claim: An excellent human form alone cannot save someone: without divine guidance and prior felicity, a person sees only himself and mistakes that for perfection, ending in the lowest state.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r5.anchor: إذا لم يصحبه توفيق وسبقته سعادة من خالقه ولم يجعل له نور يمشي به لم ير غير نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links this surah to the two preceding ones: human form seems to promise shared perfection, yet people diverge toward ascent or degradation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r1.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : هذه سورة موضحة ومتممة للمقصود

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r2.claim: Those who rise answer a divine call quickly, while people who resist follow what was written for them; each person is made ready for the end appointed to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r2.anchor: فإذا ليس يرقى من خص بمزية التقريب إلا لأنه نودي من قريب فأسرع في إجابة مناديه وأصاخ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r3.claim: A fair-minded person should know that everyone is enabled for the end they were created for and should ask God for sincerity; whoever finds good should thank God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r3.anchor: فعلى العاقل المنصف في نفسه أن يعلم أن كلا ميسر لما خلق له فيضرع إلى خالقه في طلب الإخلاص

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r4.claim: The surah explains the Prophet's abundant favors and signs of divine love: God neither forsook nor disliked him, and bestowed these gifts by grace rather than earned merit.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r4.anchor: كل ذلك فضلا منه سبحانه وتعالى وإحسانا لا لعمل تقدم يستوجب ذلك أو بعضه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r5.claim: An excellent human form alone cannot save someone: without divine guidance and prior felicity, a person sees only himself and mistakes that for perfection, ending in the lowest state.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r5.anchor: إذا لم يصحبه توفيق وسبقته سعادة من خالقه ولم يجعل له نور يمشي به لم ير غير نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p470#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p470#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p470#2/r6.claim: The contrast between the secure city and the previous place of solitude mirrors the movement from human excellence to degradation, warning Meccans against stubbornness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p470#2/r6.anchor: فيكونون بذلك قد ردوا أسفل سافلين في البلد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r1.claim: Despite humanity's excellence, God lets appetite and low desires overpower reason, turning people away from their purpose and bringing them down to the lowest state.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r1.anchor: سلط الله سبحانه وتعالى عليه شهوات وهيأ طبعه لرذائل وأخلاق دنيئات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r2.claim: Appetite blinds reason and leads people to idolatry, injustice, falsehood, and countless sins, making a human worse than animals that lack accountable reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r2.anchor: فصار بذلك أحط رتبة من البهائم بل من أدنى الحشرات المستقذرات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r3.claim: People misuse the faculties that distinguish them from animals and therefore deserve humiliating punishment; death without recompense for their wrongs makes resurrection necessary.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r3.anchor: فلا بد في الحكمة حينئذ من بعثه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r4.claim: The body is also returned to a lower state through old age: strength, dignity, knowledge, and clear thought fade, and formerly familiar people may become repelled by the elder.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p473/r4.anchor: وأما في خلقه فبالهرم حتى صار بعد تلك القوى ضعيفا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r1.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r1.claim: Ibn Burjān says spiritual degradation is disbelief and denial; in the intermediate realm a person may be transformed into the animal or vermin matching their earthly character, and in the afterlife disfigured.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r1.anchor: وقال ابن برجان : أما رده في طريق الديانة فبالكفر والتكذيب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r2.speaker: الأقليشي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r2.claim: Al-Aqlaishī says the body pulls the human downward: if intellect leads desire, a person ascends among the near; if desire leads, they descend to Hell and become remote.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو العباس الأقليشي في شرح ( المقدم المؤخر ) من شرحه للاسماء الحسنى : إن الله تعالى خلقه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r5.claim: The passage uses omission by implication: the first clause omits sinful deeds, while the exception implies preserving humanity's original, sound form.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r5.anchor: فالآية كما ترى من الاحتباك : حذف أولا بما أفهمته الآية عمل السيئات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.claim: The surah's oath recalls the Torah's account of God coming from Sinai, Seir, and Paran; ideal creation, the righteous, and the fallen summarize the Torah's beginnings, laws, and later history.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.anchor: وذلك أن قسمها هو قوله في التوراة ( أتانا ربنا من سيناء وشرق بنا من جبل ساعر , وظهر لنا من جبال فاران )

NAHHAS:v5p256/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p256/r7.claim: He interprets being returned to the lowest as reaching decrepit old age.
NAHHAS:v5p256/r7.anchor: فعن ابن عباس إلى أرذل العمر

NAHHAS:v5p256/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r8.speaker: عكرمة
NAHHAS:v5p256/r8.claim: He interprets it as being returned to the Fire.

NAHHAS:v5p256/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r9.speaker: محمد بن جرير
NAHHAS:v5p256/r9.claim: He argues that the correct interpretation is old age: the passage counts observable changes from youth to senility, not an afterlife people may deny.
NAHHAS:v5p256/r9.anchor: وزعم محمد بن جرير أن الصواب إلى أرذل العمل أي إلى الهرم ويكون هذا لخاص من الناس واستدل على صواب هذا أن الله جل وعز إنما عدد ما شاهدوه من قدرته من خروج الإنسان من الشباب إلى الهرم

NAHHAS:v5p256/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r10.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p256/r10.claim: A counterargument says this limitation is unnecessary because God's proofs and the Prophet's signs are manifest, making all revealed matters as good as witnessed.
NAHHAS:v5p256/r10.anchor: وقال غيره هذا لا يلزم لأن حجج الله ظاهرة وقد ظهرت آيات نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم فوجب أن يكون كل ما أخبر به بمنزلة المعاين

DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.claim: An explicitly weak report identifies the Fig with Syria and Olive with Palestine, Sinai with Moses' mountain, and the secure town with Mecca; it allegorizes the human as Muhammad, the lowest as idolaters, and the exception as the four caliphs.
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.anchor: فسألنا ابن عباس عن تفسيرها فقال

DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.claim: He identified the Fig as Noah's mosque on al-Judi, Olive as Jerusalem, Sinai as its mosque, and the secure town as Mecca; return to the lowest means extreme old age, excusing contemporaries whose minds failed and preserving their prior reward.
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p554/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r1.claim: He identified Fig and Olive as the Sacred Mosque and al-Aqsa, where the Night Journey ended; Sinai as Moses' mountain, Mecca as the secure town, upright stature as standing erect, and the lowest as decrepit age.
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p554/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r2.claim: He identified the Fig with Damascus's mountain and Olive with Jerusalem's, Sinai as a blessed wooded mountain and Mecca as the secure town; the oath ends at verse 4, the lowest is Hell, and the final command means be certain of God's proof.
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r2.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم وابن عساكر عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.claim: He identified the first oaths as fruit, the blessed mountain, and Mecca; human creation is in the finest image, return is to Fire, believers are excepted, and their reward is uncounted.
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.anchor: وأخرج الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد

DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.claim: He glossed finest stature as the most balanced form, return as extreme old age, and an unending reward as undiminished.
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وابن جرير وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.claim: When believers reach extreme old age, their earlier good deeds continue to be credited; age neither harms their former reward nor adds sins for later incapacity.
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.anchor: يقول: فإذا بلغ المؤمن أرذل العمر

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.claim: He glossed the finest form as the best image and the lowest state as Hell in the worst form.
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله: {لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم}

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.claim: He identified the oaths with actual figs and olives, Sinai as the blessed mountain, and Mecca; finest form is youth and strength, senility is the lowest, and the believer retains reward without reproach.
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن عكرمة

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r4.claim: He identified the oaths with actual figs and olives, finest form with a beautiful image, and the lowest with Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r4.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن الحسن

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r1.claim: Asked by Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq, he said the disbeliever descends from youth to old age and then to Hell; ʿAli's verse uses أسفل السفل for the lowest depths.
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r1.anchor: وأخرج الطستي عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق قال له

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r2.claim: His poem uses أسفل السفل for the lowest depth, supporting the phrase's meaning.
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r2.anchor: أما سمعت علي بن أبي طالب وهو يقول: فأضحوا لدى دار الجحيم

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r3.claim: He glossed the return to the lowest as extreme old age.
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r3.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن الضحاك

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r4.claim: He said Quran reciters are not returned to decrepit old age, interpreting the exception as those who recite the Quran.
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r4.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r5.claim: He reports a saying that Quran reciters avoid senility; linking it to 22:5, he says they do not reach the state of knowing nothing after knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r5.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن عكرمة

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r6.claim: He glossed the lowest as frailty without former strength and said Quran readers are not reduced to the state in 22:5; the exception refers to Quran's companions.
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r6.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم عن عكرمة

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r7.claim: He said that when old age and weakness prevent work, a person still receives the reward of earlier youthful deeds.
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r10.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r10.claim: The Prophet said the recording angel continues to credit good deeds when a person weakens and withholds bad deeds; a Quran reciter is spared senility and ignorance.
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r10.anchor: وأخرج الحكيم الترمذي في نوادر الأصول عن أنس عن النبي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says people are returned to senility until their minds fail.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r5.anchor: لقد خلقنا الانسان في احسن تقويم ثم رددناه اسفل سافلين يقول : يرد إلى ارذل العمر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies the fig and olive as edible fruit, Sinai as the blessed Mount, and Mecca as the secure city; he reads best form as finest shape, the lowest state as Hell, and the believers' reward as uncounted.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد والتين والزيتون قال : الفاكهة التي ياكل الناس وطور سينين قال : الطور الجبل وسينين المبارك وهذا البلد الامين قال : مكة لقد خلقنا الانسان في احسن تقويم قال : في احسن صورة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says old age and weakness reduce a person's ability to work, but God grants the same reward as in youth.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ثم رددناه اسفل سافلين يقول : إلى الكبر وضعفه ، فاذا ضعف وكبر عن العمل كتب له مثل اجر ما كان يعمل في شبيبته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r3.claim: Ikrimah says the lowest state is advanced age.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r3.anchor: ثم رددناه اسفل سافلين قال : رد إلى ارذل العمر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says the best form is the finest appearance, while the lowest state is the Fire in the worst appearance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : لقد خلقنا الانسان في احسن تقويم يقول : في احسن صورة ثم رددناه اسفل سافلين قال : في النار في شر صورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.claim: The surah presents Islam as humanity's sound primordial nature and treats departures from its foundations as corruption and misguidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.anchor: احتوت هذه السورة على التنبيه بأن الله خلق الإنسان على الفطرة المستقيمة ليعلموا أن الإسلام هو الفطرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r4.claim: The constitution and subsequent return are subtle, inward matters requiring reflection, so the oath's emphatic force is apt when most people act as if they deny their natural disposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r4.anchor: والقسم عليه يدل على أن التقويم تقويم خفي وأن الرد رد خفي يجب التدبر لإدراكه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r5.claim: Reading the best constitution as bodily form and the return as old age does not fit the surah's purpose or warrant its emphatic oath.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r5.anchor: وأما خلق جسد الإنسان في أحسن تقويم فلا ارتباط له بمقصد السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r1.claim: To fit the old-age interpretation to the surah's aim, one would have to read the lowering as an ungrateful response to a blessing that brings a person low.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r1.anchor: ولا يلائم مقصد السورة إلا أن يتأول بأن ذلك ذكر نعمة على الإنسان عكس الإنسان شكرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r7.claim: The clause about being returned low is coordinated with creation and remains under the oath; its pronoun refers to the human defined in either of the two earlier senses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r7.anchor: وجملة : { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } معطوفة على جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r8.claim: Thumma marks a higher-order delay: reversal from the best created state to the lowest is startling, and changing an existing state is more astonishing than originating one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r8.anchor: و { ثم } لإفادة التراخي الرتبي كما هو شأنها في عطف الجمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r1.claim: The phrase means that God made the human low or placed him among the lowest; radd figuratively means turning something into a different state.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r2.claim: Asfal is a superlative for the most base, and “lowest of the low” means low in belief in the Creator, as the next exception for believers indicates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r2.anchor: فالمراد : أسفل سافلين في الإعتقاد بخالقه بقرينة قوله : { إلا الذين آمنوا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r3.claim: Sufliyya literally means low location but commonly signifies baseness of character; the phrase is the second object of radd, construed like verbs of becoming.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r3.anchor: وحقيقة السفالة : انخفاض المكان ، وتطلق مجازا شائعا على الخسة والحقارة في النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r4.claim: People fall from their innate monotheism and reverent awareness by worshipping stones, animals, trees, time, or denying the Maker despite seeing creation and themselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r4.anchor: من بقر أو تماسيح أو ثعابين أو من شجر السمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r5.claim: The author contrasts denial of the Creator with the reminder to look within oneself for signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r5.anchor: أو من يجحد وجود الصانع وهو يشاهد مصنوعاته ويحس بوجود نفسه قال تعالى : { وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r6.claim: Human ethical degradation includes flattering from greed, stinginess from fear, panic, sacrificing people to idols, burying daughters, and burning widows with dead husbands.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r6.anchor: فمن ملق إذا طمع ، ومن شح إذا شجع ، ومن جزع إذا خاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r7.claim: Attributing the return to God is figurative: He establishes high-level causes and their interactions that lead through subsidiary causes to immediate causes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r7.anchor: وإسناد الرد إلى الله تعالى إسناد مجازي لأنه يكون الأسباب العالية ونظام تفاعلها وتقابلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r8.claim: This is like attributing the extension and gradual withdrawal of a shadow to God, or saying a prince built a city.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r8.anchor: على نحو إسناد مد وقبض الظل إليه تعالى في قوله : { ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r1.claim: Alternatively, asfal safilin is an adverbial place lower than the lowest inhabitants, the abode of punishment; on this reading radd means placing someone where deserved and God's agency is literal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { أسفل سافلين } ظرفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r2.claim: The place reading is the lowest part of the Fire, as in the verse about hypocrites being in its lowest depth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r2.anchor: وذلك هو دار العذاب كقوله : { إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Uways recounts Rabiʿa asking Malik who is base: Malik answered one who earns through religion, and the basest of the base exploits others' religion; Rabiʿa approved.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r3.anchor: قال ابن أبي أويس : قال مالك : أقبل علي يوما ربيعة فقال لي : من السفلة يا مالك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r4.claim: The author links this teaching to polytheists whose leaders misled them into idol worship to secure their own leadership.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r4.anchor: وأن المشركين كانوا أسفل سافلين لأنهم ضللهم كبراؤهم وأيمتهم فسولوا لهم عبادة الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r5.claim: The exception is connected to the general term “human”: nonbelievers remain low, while people who believe return from shirk to their original fitra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r5.anchor: استثناء متصل من عموم الإنسان فلما أخبر عن الإنسان بأنه رد أسفل سافلين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r8.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة والضحاك والنخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r8.claim: These authorities interpret the lowest state as old age, loss of reason, and failing memory; the believer is exempt from the duty of action.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r8.anchor: فقال عكرمة وقتادة والضحاك والنخعي: معناه بالهرم وذهول العقل وتفلت الفكر حتى يصير لا يعلم شيئا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls this a sound reading but says it affects only some humans, as an instructive sign.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r9.anchor: وهذا قول حسن وليس المعنى أن كل إنسان يعتريه هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r10.claim: Ibn Masud reads al-safilin with the definite article.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r12.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد وأبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r12.claim: These commentators say the lowest state is Hell for a person who persists in disbelief; the believing are a separate exception.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد وأبو العالية: المعنى رددناه أسفل سافلين في النار على كفره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن العوفي، عكرمة، إبراهيم، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r2.claim: Asfal sāfilīn can mean extreme old age; al-Ḍaḥḥāk describes old age as weakness after youth and strength, below the weak, sick, children, and elderly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r2.anchor: إلى أرذل العمر رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس وبه قال عكرمة وإبراهيم وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r3.claim: The plural sāfilīn agrees with al-insān understood generically; Arabic allows either singular or plural agreement depending on whether an individual is intended.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r3.anchor: وإنما قال سافلين على الجمع لأن الإنسان في معنى جمع تقول هذا أفضل قائم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r4.speaker: الحسن وأبو العالية ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r4.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means that some people are cast into the Fire; the wording need not mean that every bit of a person's wealth is spent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r4.anchor: إلى النار قاله الحسن وأبو العالية ومجاهد والمعنى إنا نفعل هذا بكثير من الناس

IBNKATHIR:95:5/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r1.speaker: مجاهد وأبو العالية والحسن وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r1.anchor: قاله مجاهد ،   وأبو العالية ،   والحسن ،   وابن زيد ،   وغيرهم .

IBNKATHIR:95:5/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r2.claim: After the beauty and vitality of creation, the human's destination is the Fire if he does not obey God and follow the messengers; this sets up the exception for believers.
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r2.anchor: ثم بعد هذا الحسن والنضارة مصيره إلى النار إن لم يطع الله ويتبع الرسل

IBNKATHIR:95:5/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r3.claim: An alternative interpretation is return to the lowest stage of life, extreme old age; ʿIkrima says one who memorizes the Qur'an is not returned to it.
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r3.anchor: روي هذا عن ابن عباس ،   وعكرمة - حتى قال عكرمة : من جمع القرآن لم يُرَدّ إلى أرذل العمر

IBNKATHIR:95:5/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r4.claim: Ibn Jarīr prefers the old-age interpretation.

IBNKATHIR:95:5/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r5.claim: The old-age interpretation does not fit the exception, since believers too may become elderly; the intended meaning is the Fire, as in the exception in al-ʿAṣr.
IBNKATHIR:95:5/r5.anchor: ولو كان هذا هو المراد لما حَسُن استثناء المؤمنين من ذلك ؛ لأن الهَرَم قد يصيبُ بعضهم ،   وإنما المراد ما ذكرناه

JISHUMI:v10p7469/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7469/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
JISHUMI:v10p7469/r4.claim: He reads asfal al-sāfilīn with the definite article, unlike the common form without it.
JISHUMI:v10p7469/r4.anchor: وقراءة العامة: (أسفل سافلين)، وعن ابن مسعود: (أسفل السافلين)

KASHSHAF:95:5/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:95:5/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:95:5/r1.claim: Because people failed to thank God for their excellent creation, they may be returned lower than the lowest in form, as ugly and misshapen people of Hell, or to the lowest ranks of Hell.
KASHSHAF:95:5/r1.anchor: حين لم يشكر نعمة تلك الخلقة الحسنة القويمة السوية : أن رددناه أسفل من سفل خلقاً وتركيباً

KASHSHAF:95:5/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:95:5/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:95:5/r2.claim: Alternatively, God returns people below their former beauty through old age: bent backs, white hair, wrinkled skin, weakened senses and strength, slow gait, faint voice, and senility.
KASHSHAF:95:5/r2.anchor: فقوس ظهره بعد اعتداله ،   وابيض شعره بعد سواده ،   وتشنن جلده

KASHSHAF:95:5/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:95:5/r3.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF:95:5/r3.claim: Abd Allah reads the phrase as 'the lowest of the low.'

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r12.claim: أسفل سافلين may mean the ugliest form and composition, the people of Hell, or the lowest of its ranks; alternatively it describes reversal in old age, with a bent back, white hair, wrinkled skin, dulled senses, weak strength, and failing judgment. Abdullah reads أسفل السافلين.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r12.anchor: أن رددناه أسفل من سفل خلقا وتركيبا ، يعني : أقبح من قبح صورة

SAMIN-DURR:95:5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:95:5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:95:5/r1.claim: ‘Asfala safilin’ may be a circumstantial modifying the object, or an adjective of an omitted place (‘a place lower than the lowest’).
SAMIN-DURR:95:5/r1.anchor: يجوز فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه حال من المفعول. والثاني: أنه صفة لمكان محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:95:5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:95:5/r2.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:95:5/r2.claim: ‘Abd Allah reads ‘al-safilin’ with the definite article.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r25.speaker: الضحاك، الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r25.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi say the return to the lowest is old age after youth and weakness after strength; lowest here means after completeness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r25.anchor: أحدهما : إلى الهرم بعد الشباب , والضعف بعد القوة , قاله الضحاك والكلبي , ويكون أسفل بمعنى بعد التمام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r26.speaker: مجاهد، أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r26.claim: Mujahid and Abu al-Aliya interpret it as falling into disbelief, with the lowest levels meaning the bottom of Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r26.anchor: قاله مجاهد وأبو العالية , ويكون أسفل السافلين محمولا على الدرك الأسفل من النار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r27.claim: Mawardi also allows a decline in discernment after it had been strong.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r27.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : إلى ضعف التمييز بعد قوته .

MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the best form is the most upright creation, the return to the lowest is decrepit old age, and the reward of the faithful is undiminished.
MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ﴿ في أحسن تقويم ﴾ قال يعني في أعدل خلق ﴿ ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين ﴾ يعني إلى أرذل العمر

MUJAHID:v2p770/r5.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p770/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p770/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets being returned to the lowest as excepting the one who believes.
MUJAHID:v2p770/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ في أحسن تقويم ﴾ يعني في أحسن خلق ﴿ ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين ﴾ يعني إلا من آمن

MUQATIL:95:1-6/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:95:1-6/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:95:1-6/r3.claim: After youth and beauty, people may fall to the lowest form as their brows droop and youth, mind, strength, voice, and appearance disappear.
MUQATIL:95:1-6/r3.anchor: { ثم رددناه } بعد الشباب والصورة الحسنة { أسفل سافلين } [آية: 5]

NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r1.claim: One interpretation says the ungrateful person is reduced below the lowest in form and composition, becoming uglier than the ugly, namely the people of the Fire.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r1.anchor: حين لم يشكر نعمة تلك الخلقة الحسنة القويمة السوية أن رددناه أسفل من سفل خلقا وتركيبا يعنى أقبح من قبح صورة وهم أصحاب النار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r2.claim: Alternatively, he is reduced below the lowest ranks, to the people of the lowest degrees.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r2.anchor: أو أسفل من سفل من أهل الدركات

NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r3.claim: Alternatively, after being formed and improved, a person declines in old age: the back bends, hair turns white, skin wrinkles, senses fail, gait slows, and strength and courage weaken.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r3.anchor: حيث نكسناه فى خلقه فقوس ظهره بعد اعتداله وأبيض شعره بعد سواده وتشنن جلده وكل سمعه وبصره وتغير كل شئ منه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r4.claim: This decline brings the person to old age and senility, with hardship and diminished ability to worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#6/r4.anchor: فمشيه دليف وصونه حفات وقوته ضعف وشهامته خوف

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r9.speaker: الضحاك والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, and others take the lowest low as decrepit old age after youth, weakness after strength, and a return to childlike condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r9.anchor: إلى أرذل العمر، وهو الهرم بعد الشباب، والضعف بعد القوة، حتى يصير كالصبي في الحال الأول قاله الضحاك

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r10.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن أبي نجيح
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r10.claim: Mujahid, via Ibn Abi Najih, says the lowest low is Hell, referring to the disbeliever.
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r10.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } إلى النار، يعني الكافر، وقاله أبو العالية.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r11.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r11.claim: Abu al-Aliya also interprets the lowest low as Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r11.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } إلى النار، يعني الكافر، وقاله أبو العالية.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r1.claim: One explanation says that humans, after their exalted construction, become arrogant enough to claim divinity; God lowers them through bodily filth until they recognize their created nature and return to His decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: لما وصفه الله بتلك الصفات الجليلة التي ركب الإنسان عليها، طغى وعلا، حتى قال: أنا ربكم الأعلى

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r2.claim: Abdullah reads the phrase with the definite plural, asfal al-safilin.
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله «أسفل السافلين». وقال: «أسفل سافلين» على الجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r3.claim: The plural form is justified because insan has a collective sense; singular wording could also have been used, and plural reference to insan appears elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r3.anchor: وقال: «أسفل سافلين» على الجمع لأن الإنسان في معنى جمع، ولو قال: أسفل سافل جاز

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r4.claim: Another reading takes being returned to the lowest low as being returned to error, as the next surah says humanity is in loss except believers and good-doers.
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5#2/r4.anchor: وقد قيل: إن معنى { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } أي رددناه إلى الضلال

QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r1.claim: The descent concerns spiritual qualities, which can sink when a person abandons innate nature and faith; bodily form itself does not descend in this way.
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r1.anchor: فهي التي تنتكس إلى أسفل سافلين حين ينحرف عن الفطرة ويحيد عن الإيمان

QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r2.claim: Human spiritual capacity can rise beyond the angels, as in the Ascension when Gabriel stopped while Muhammad rose to the highest station.
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r2.anchor: وارتفع محمد بن عبد الله - الإنسان - إلى المقام الأسنى

QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r3.claim: If the human being falls, animals become better and more upright because they remain true to their nature, praise God, and fulfill their earthly role, while people may reject God and follow desire.
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r3.anchor: حيث تصبح البهائم أرفع منه وأقوم ، لاستقامتها على فطرتها

QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r4.claim: The human being begins with sound nature and capacity but sinks when turning from the guidance God showed, left to choose between the two paths.
QUTB-ZILAL:95:5/r4.anchor: حين ينحرف بهذه الفطرة عن الخط الذي هداه الله إليه ، وبينه له ، وتركه ليختار أحد النجدين

RAZI:95:5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:95:5/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the return to the lowest state as reaching decrepit old age, as in the verse about being returned to the most feeble age.
RAZI:95:5/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد أرذل العمر

RAZI:95:5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:5/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
RAZI:95:5/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the lowest are the weak, infirm, helpless people; old age weakens hearing, sight, reason, and ability, leaving one unable to do good.
RAZI:95:5/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : السافلون هم الضعفاء والزمنى ، ومن لا يستطيع حيلة ولا يجد سبيلا

RAZI:95:5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:5/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:95:5/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ says singular أسفل سافل would be grammatically possible, but the plural is used because الإنسان is singular in wording and plural in meaning.
RAZI:95:5/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء : ولو كانت أسفل سافل لكان صوابا ، لأن لفظ الإنسان واحد

RAZI:95:5/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:5/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:95:5/r4.claim: The plural-by-meaning construction is paralleled by a verse that shifts from singular wording about one who brings truth to plural “those” who are mindful.
RAZI:95:5/r4.anchor: والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به أولئك هم المتقون

RAZI:95:5/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:5/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:95:5/r5.claim: He also cites a verse that begins with singular الإنسان and shifts to plural pronouns.
RAZI:95:5/r5.anchor: وإنا إذا أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة فرح بها وإن تصبهم

RAZI:95:5/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:5/r6.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
RAZI:95:5/r6.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan interpret the lowest state as being returned to the Fire.
RAZI:95:5/r6.anchor: والقول الثاني : ما ذكره مجاهد والحسن ثم رددناه إلى النار

RAZI:95:5/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:5/r7.speaker: علي
RAZI:95:5/r7.claim: Ali says Hell’s gates are arranged one below another and the lowest level is filled first, explaining the phrase as the lowest of the low.
RAZI:95:5/r7.anchor: قال علي عليه السلام : وضع أبواب جهنم بعضها أسفل من بعض فيبدأ بالأسفل فيملأ

ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r5.claim: One interpretation of being returned to the lowest of the low is decrepit old age.

ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r6.claim: Another interpretation is misguidance, supported by the statement that humanity is in loss except those who believe and do good.
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r6.anchor: وقيل إلى الضلال كما قال عز وجل: (إن الإنسان لفي خسر

ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r7.claim: He prefers that humanity was created upon the natural disposition, and whoever disbelieves and strays is returned to the lowest of the low.
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r7.anchor: وهو - والله أعلم - أن خلق الخلق على الفطرة

RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads the lowest state as decrepit old age, when hearing, sight, reason, ability, and good works weaken.
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد أرذل العمر

RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the low as the weak, chronically ill, helpless people who cannot find a way or means.
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : السافلون هم الضعفاء والزمني

RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains the plural سافلين despite singular الإنسان by treating humanity as a collective, like other singular nouns that denote a group.
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء : ولو كانت أسفل سافل لكان صوابا

RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r4.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r4.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan read the lowest state as Hell; ʿAli says its gates are stacked, with the lowest filled first.
RAZI-FULL:v32p12/r4.anchor: ما ذكره مجاهد والحسن ثم رددناه إلى النار

STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.claim: Al-Tīn is likely an early-middle Makkan sūrah revealed after Sūrah 85, though some consider it Madinan; it is named for the fig in verse 1.
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.anchor: A Makkan sūrah, al-Tīn was most likely revealed in the early part of the middle Makkan period, shortly after Sūrah 85

STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.claim: Verses 4–6 describe humanity's exalted origin and fall when people fail to live by their true nature, a message like 103:2–3.
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.anchor: The main theme is found in vv. 4–6, which are among the most famous verses in the Quran. They speak to the human condition

STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.claim: A further view makes the fig the Garden leaves Adam and Eve used to cover themselves and the olive the blessed tree; these may foreshadow human abasement and intellect's light.
STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.anchor: Others say that the fig refers to the leaves of the Garden (7:22), with which Adam and Eve covered themselves, and the olive refers to the blessed olive tree in 24:35

STUDYQURAN:95:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r1.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r1.claim: Outwardly, the verse can mean old age, when faculties diminish, sometimes into decrepitude, as in the parallel about long life causing regression.
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r1.anchor: With regard to the outward human form, this verse can be seen as a reference to old age, when faculties are diminished, sometimes to the point of decrepitude

STUDYQURAN:95:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r2.claim: Inwardly, it can mean people fall below their true nature and are cast into the Fire for failing the demands of their beautiful creation.
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r2.anchor: With regard to the inner reality, it can be taken as a reference to human beings falling below their true nature and consequently being cast into the Fire

STUDYQURAN:95:5/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r3.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r3.claim: The phrase can describe disbelievers, who are lower than cattle, or the place into which they are cast.
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r3.anchor: the lowest of the low can be understood as a reference to the state of disbelievers, of whom 7:179 says, Such as these are like cattle

STUDYQURAN:95:5/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r4.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r4.claim: Some read the phrase as “the lowest, lowly,” with lowly describing abasement and implying that the condemned condition itself brought them down.
STUDYQURAN:95:5/r4.anchor: According to some, the lowest of the low should be read

ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed after surah 85, The Great Constellations.

ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.claim: It states a fundamental moral truth shared by all true religious teachings.
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.anchor: formulates a fundamental moral verity, stressing the fact that it is common to all true religious teachings

ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n3/r1.claim: The fall results from humans corrupting their original positive disposition through their own actions and omissions.
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n3/r1.anchor: consequence of man's betrayal - in another word, corruption - of his original, positive disposition

ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n3/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n3/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n3/r2.claim: Asad directs readers to his note on 2:7 for the attribution of this reduction to God's action.
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n3/r2.anchor: Regarding the attribution, by God, of this "reduction" to His Own doing, see note 7 on 2:7

TAB-FULL:v24p514/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Ikrima, explains the descent to the lowest state as return to decrepit old age.
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: «إلى أرذل العمر»

TAB-FULL:v24p514/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that some people in the Prophet's time became senile; when asked about their lost understanding, God excused them and preserved the reward earned before their minds failed.
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] يقول: يرد إلى أرذل العمر، كبر حتى ذهب عقله، وهم نفر ردوا إلى أرذل العمر

TAB-FULL:v24p514/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r3.claim: Ikrima says people are returned to the most decrepit age.
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r3.anchor: عن أبي رجاء، قال: سئل عكرمة، عن قوله: {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: «ردوا إلى أرذل العمر»

TAB-FULL:v24p514/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r4.claim: Ibrahim interprets the phrase as return to decrepit old age.
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r4.anchor: عن حماد، عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: «إلى أرذل العمر»

TAB-FULL:v24p514/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r5.claim: Qatadah glosses the lowest state as senility.
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: «رددناه إلى الهرم»

TAB-FULL:v24p514/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r6.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r6.claim: Ikrima says old age does not harm a person who ends life doing the best deeds he used to do.
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة، {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: «الشيخ الهرم، لم يضره كبره أن ختم الله له بأحسن ما كان يعمل»

TAB-FULL:v24p514/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r7.claim: A second view takes the verse as return to Hell in the ugliest form; Abu al-Aliyah specifies the form of a pig.
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r7.anchor: عن أبي جعفر الرازي، عن الربيع بن أنس، عن أبي العالية، {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: «في شر صورة في صورة خنزير»

TAB-FULL:v24p515/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r1.claim: Mujahid repeatedly interprets the lowest state as Hell.
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: «النار»

TAB-FULL:v24p515/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r2.claim: Hasan explains the lowest state as Hell, the person's abode.
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: قال الحسن: «جهنم مأواه»

TAB-FULL:v24p515/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse means return to Hell.
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: «إلى النار»

TAB-FULL:v24p515/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers return to decrepit old age, when senility and weakness undo the vigor of youth; this visible change supports God's power to resurrect the dead, as the next argument states.
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r4.anchor: معناه: ثم رددناه إلى أرذل العمر، إلى عمر الخرفى، الذين ذهبت عقولهم من الهرم والكبر

TAB-FULL:v24p515/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r5.claim: His proof is that the audience denies the threatened Hell but has witnessed people age from healthy strength into weakness and senility, so the argument appeals to what they see or acknowledge.
TAB-FULL:v24p515/r5.anchor: وكان القوم للنار التي كان الله يتوعدهم بها في الآخرة منكرين، وكانوا لأهل الهرم والخرف من بعد الشباب والجلد شاهدين

TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.claim: Some interpreters treat the exception as connected to the generic singular ‘human’: it has collective meaning, like ‘humanity is in loss’ in 103:2, so believers may be excepted and a superlative may be related to a plural group.
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.anchor: لأن الإنسان وإن كان في لفظ واحد، فإنه في معنى الجمع، لأنه بمعنى الجنس، كما قيل: {والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر} [العصر: 2]

TAB-FULL:v24p517/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r2.claim: Ikrima says a person who recites the Quran is not returned to decrepit old age, and reads the phrase as senility so severe that one no longer knows after having known.
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: " كان يقال: من قرأ القرآن لم يرد إلى أرذل العمر، ثم قرأ: {لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} [التين: 5]

TAB-FULL:v24p517/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r3.claim: Others say even believers may reach old age; the exception concerns those whose minds fail, whose deeds cease, and who can no longer add good, while their former good works continue to count.
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r3.anchor: قالوا: وإنما استثنى قوله: {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} [التين: 6] من معنى مضمر في قوله: {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5]

TAB-FULL:v24p517/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r4.claim: Al-Tabari allows a disconnected exception: even after being returned to the lowest state, believers who did righteous deeds retain their reward.
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r4.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون قوله: {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} [التين: 6] استثناء منقطعا

TAB-FULL:v24p519/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says a believer who becomes unable to continue a righteous practice in old age keeps receiving its reward until death.
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم أجر غير ممنون} [التين: 6] قال: «فأيما رجل كان يعمل عملا صالحا وهو قوي شاب، فعجز عنه، جرى له أجر ذلك العمل حتى يموت»

TAB-FULL:v24p519/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says obedience maintained throughout youth earns the same reward after the believer grows senile, without liability for acts committed after losing reason.
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r2.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس: {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم أجر غير ممنون} [التين: 6] يقول: «إذا كان يعمل بطاعة الله في شبيبته كلها

TAB-FULL:v24p519/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r3.claim: Ibrahim says a believer who reaches decrepit age receives the reward of the best work he did in youth and health.
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r3.anchor: عن حماد، عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] قال: " إلى أرذل العمر، فإذا بلغ المؤمن إلى أرذل العمر، كتب له كأحسن ما كان يعمل في شبابه وصحته، فهو قوله: {فلهم أجر غير ممنون} [التين: 6]

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r1.claim: Ikrima says God pays the believer's reward or deed and does not hold him to account when old age returns him to weakness.
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r1.anchor: عن أبي رجاء، قال: سئل عكرمة، عن قوله: {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم أجر غير ممنون} [التين: 6] قال: «يوفيه الله أجره أو عمله، ولا يؤاخذه إذا رد إلى أرذل العمر»

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r2.claim: Ikrima says senility does not harm an elderly person if God ends his life upon the best deeds he used to do.
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} [التين: 6] قال: «الشيخ الهرم لم يضره كبره إن ختم الله له بأحسن ما كان يعمل»

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r3.claim: Qatadah says a person who reaches old age after doing good receives the same reward he had while able to work.
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} [التين: 6] قال: من أدركه الهرم، وكان يعمل صالحا، كان له مثل أجره

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the descent as Hell and exempts believers from that fate; Mujahid glosses the exception as those who believe.
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا} [التين: 6] : إلا من آمن

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.claim: Hasan reads the exception after Hell as parallel to the exception of believers from loss in Surat al-Asr.
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.anchor: قال الحسن، في قوله: {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] : «في النار» {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} [التين: 6]

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r6.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that people return to decrepit age, while believers who did righteous work in health and youth retain its reward in old age.
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r6.anchor: قول من قال: معناه: ثم رددناه إلى أرذل العمر، {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} [التين: 6] في حال صحتهم وشبابهم

CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r1.claim: A transmitted variant reads the phrase with a definite article: ʾasfala s-sāfilīn.
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Tradiert wird auch die determinierte Lesung ʾasfala s-sāfilīn

CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r2.claim: Although ʾasfal literally means lowest, it can figuratively mean powerless or subordinate; the author takes it here as human senility, supported by Quranic uses and commentators.
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Die wörtliche Bedeutung von ʾasfal ist eine räumliche: „zuunterst, unten befindlich“. Im übertragenen Sinne kann das Wort dann auch Ohnmacht und Unterlegenheit beschreiben
