CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Birkeland
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r3.claim: Birkeland says the phrase's exceptional humiliation must mean the damned in Hell, not ordinary old age; the author rejects this because Arabic poetry disparages aging and radda supports the aging sense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:5:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Birkeland zwar geltend, die durch den Ausdruck ʾasfala sāfilīn ausgedrückte „ganz außerordentliche Erniedrigung“ könne nur der Zustand der Verdammten in der Hölle

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.claim: The oath's answer fits the preceding places of revelation: it describes humanity's beginning in the best form and its eventual return to the lowest state.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.anchor: فإنه أقسم بالراسالات على بداية الإنسان ونهايته

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.claim: People divide into those who accept the prophetic call and those who refuse it; most are returned low, while believers receive reward.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.anchor: ثم لما كان الناس في إجابة هذه الدعوة فريقين منهم مَنْ أجاب ومنهم من أبى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r4.claim: God is also named as the one who returns people low to emphasize divine control over both the beginning and end of human life.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r4.anchor: أراد أن يذكر أن بيده البداية والنهاية، وأنه القادر أولاً وأخيراً لا معقب لحكمه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r5.claim: Had the verse said people were returned low in the passive, it could suggest another agent undoes God's creation.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r5.anchor: لكان يفهم ذاك أن هناك ردّاً غيره يفسدُ خلقته ويهدم ما بناه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r7.claim: Thumma marks temporal delay before the low state and a great difference in rank between the best form and the lowest state.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r7.anchor: فهي من حيث الوقت تفيد التراخي، كما أنها من حيث الرتبة تفيد التراخي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r8.speaker: مفسرون
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r8.claim: One interpretation takes asfal sāfilīn as extreme old age, with physical and mental decline until the person knows nothing.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r8.anchor: الهرم وضَعْف القُوى الظاهرة والباطنة وذهول العقل حتى يصير لا يعلم شيئاً

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r11.speaker: مفسرون
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes asfal sāfilīn as the lowest places, Hell or its lowest level; the exception then straightforwardly excludes the righteous.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r11.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أن المقصود به أسفل الأماكن السافلة وهو جهنم أو الدرك الأسفل من النار

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r12.claim: Fī Ẓilāl al-Qurʾān focuses on spiritual capacities: rejecting faith reverses humanity's potential to rise above angels, making it fall below animals that follow their nature.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r12.anchor: والتركيز في هذا المقام على خصائصه الروحية. فهي التي تنتكس إلى أسفل سافلين

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r14.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r14.claim: The verse can encompass all these interpretations of the lowest state.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r14.anchor: وظاهر أن معنى الآية يتسع لكل ما ذكروه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r15.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r15.claim: The nonbeliever's life is also low, distressed, and unhappy, as shown by Qur'anic descriptions of a constricted life and a fall into a remote place.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r15.anchor: وهي تفيد أيضاً أن حياة غير المؤمن نكد وغم، وعيشة ضنك وشقاء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r3.claim: The judgment argument is tightly connected to the preceding account of human creation and decline.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r3.anchor: فانظر جلالة ارتباط هذا الكلام بما قبله

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r12.claim: The verse endings were chosen to carry several meanings at once: al-amīn joins safety and trust, asfal sāfilīn old age and Hell, ghayr mamnūn lasting and unreproached reward, dīn religion and recompense, and aḥkam al-ḥākimīn wisdom and judgment.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r12.anchor: ثم انظر إلى التنسيق الجميل في اختيار خواتم الآي

TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the bodily-aging reading because it conflicts with the apparently connected exception: creation and aging apply generally to believers and unbelievers alike.
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يلائمه ما في قوله { إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات } من الاستثناء الظاهر

TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.speaker: unnamed view
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.claim: Another view limits the human to the unbeliever and reads the return as casting him into Hell or reversing his bodily form, making the exception disconnected.
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.anchor: وكذا القول بأن المراد بالإنسان هو الكافر والمراد بالرد رده إلى جهنم

TABRISI:95:4-6/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:95:4-6/r4.claim: Being returned to the lowest state means fear, decrepit old age, diminished reason, and the weakness of the infirm, children, and elderly.
TABRISI:95:4-6/r4.anchor: يريد إلى الخوف وأرذل العمر ونقصان العقل والسافلون هم الضعفاء والزمنى والأطفال

TABRISI:95:4-6/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r5.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:95:4-6/r5.claim: Another interpretation sends people back to Hell; al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and al-Jubbaʾi apply it to unbelievers.
TABRISI:95:4-6/r5.anchor: معناه ثم رددناه إلى النار عن الحسن ومجاهد وابن زيد والجبائي

TABRISI:95:4-6/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:95:4-6/r6.claim: On the Hell reading, God first created unbelievers free, rational, and accountable, but they disbelieved and were returned to the worst state.
TABRISI:95:4-6/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا فالمراد به الكفار أي خلقناهم في أحسن خلقة أحرارا عقلاء مكلفين

THALABI:v10p239/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p239/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p239/r16.claim: The lowering means return to decrepit old age, when life declines, the body weakens, and the mind departs.
THALABI:v10p239/r16.anchor: يعني إلى أرذل العمر، ينقص عمره ويضعف بدنه ويذهب عقله

THALABI:v10p239/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p239/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p239/r17.claim: Some people reached extreme old age in the Prophet’s time, and God revealed an excuse for them and promised the reward of their earlier deeds.
THALABI:v10p239/r17.anchor: قال ابن عباس: [إن] نفرا ردوا إلى أرذل العمر على عهد رسول الله

THALABI:v10p240/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r1.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v10p240/r1.claim: Extreme age does not harm an old person if God ends his life in the best state of deeds.
THALABI:v10p240/r1.anchor: قال عكرمة: لم يضر هذا الشيخ الهرم كبره إذا ختم الله تعالى له بأحسن ما كان يعمل

THALABI:v10p240/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v10p240/r2.claim: They say the lowly include the weak, elderly, and chronically ill; the indefinite phrase generalizes the whole class, unlike a definite form referring to known people.
THALABI:v10p240/r2.anchor: السافلون: الضعفى والهرمى والزمنى، فقوله (أسفل سافلين) نكرة تعم الجنس

THALABI:v10p240/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r3.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p240/r3.claim: A report from Anas says children’s good deeds benefit parents before puberty and sins are unrecorded; later, at extreme senility, the same good deeds as in health are recorded and sins omitted.
THALABI:v10p240/r3.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «المولود حتى يبلغ الحنث ما عمل من حسنة كتبت لوالديه

THALABI:v10p240/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r4.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
THALABI:v10p240/r4.claim: They interpret the return to the lowest state as a return to Hell.
THALABI:v10p240/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة: يعني ثم رددناه الى النار

THALABI:v10p240/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v10p240/r5.claim: He says the person is returned to the fire in the worst form, as a pig.
THALABI:v10p240/r5.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: يعني إلى النار في شر صورة، في صورة خنزير

THALABI:v10p240/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r6.speaker: علي
THALABI:v10p240/r6.claim: He says Hell’s gates are arranged below one another and filled from the lowest, explaining the lowest of the low.
THALABI:v10p240/r6.anchor: عن علي قال: أبواب جهنم بعضها أسفل من بعض، فيبدأ بالأسفل فيملأ

THALABI:v10p240/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r7.speaker: مصحف عبد الله
THALABI:v10p240/r7.claim: Abdullah’s codex reads the phrase with the definite article: ‘the lowest of the low.’
THALABI:v10p240/r7.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله، (أسفل السافلين) بالألف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء والكلبي وإبراهيم وعكرمة ومقاتل وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r1.claim: They say the human is returned to the most decrepit age, that is, old age.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، والكلبي: يريد أرذل العمر (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r2.claim: The lowest people include the weak, chronically ill, children, and those unable to act; senility diminishes faculties and prevents good works, as in the return to decrepit age.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: السافلون هم الضعفاء، والزمنى (¬6) (¬7)، والأطفال، ومن لا يستطيع حيلة، ولا يجد سبيلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r3.claim: Although al-insan is singular, safilin is plural because the human is meant collectively; he illustrates singular and plural agreement with other verses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: ولو كانت أسفل سافل لكان صوابا؛ لأن لفظ الإنسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وأبو العالية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r4.claim: They give another interpretation: the human is returned to Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r4.anchor: وفي الآية قول آخر، قال مجاهد: ثم رددناه إلى النار (¬7)، وهو قول الحسن (¬8)، وأبي العالية (¬9)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r5.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r5.claim: Hell's gates lie beneath one another and are filled beginning from the lowest, which explains the lowest of the low.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r5.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه: أبواب جهنم بعضها أسفل بعض، فيبتدأ بالأسفل فيملأ، وهي أسفل سافلين (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r6.claim: On the Hell interpretation, the phrase means returned to the lowest place, in the lowest of the low; the following exception of believers supports this reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p153#2/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا يكون التقدير: ثم رددناه إلى أسفل، أي في أسفل سافلين، ويدل على هذا القول استثناؤه المؤمنين

WAHIDI-QT:95:5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:95:5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:95:5/r1.claim: The decline is to extreme old age; the lowly are the aged, chronically ill, and weak.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:95:1-6/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:95:1-6/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:95:1-6/r4.claim: One interpretation takes the lowest of the low to mean extreme old age, when people become elderly, chronically ill, or weak.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:95:1-6/r4.anchor: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } إلى أرذل العمر، والسافلون: هم الهرمى والزمنى والضعفى.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r3.claim: God is also explicitly the one who returns humanity to the lowest state, showing that He controls both beginning and end; a passive verb might imply a different agent ruined His creation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r3.anchor: أراد أن يذكر أن بيده البداية والنهاية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r3.claim: Some exegetes take “the lowest of the low” as decrepit old age, with physical and mental decline and loss of understanding.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r3.anchor: فذهب قسم من المفسرين إلى أن المقصود به أرذل العمر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r5.claim: Other exegetes understand the lowest state as the lowest place, Hell or its lowest level.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r5.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أن المقصود به أسفل الأماكن السافلة وهو جهنم

ELMALILI:95:5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:5/r1.claim: Thumma ordinarily marks temporal delay; he rejects a purely rank-based reading if it means some people never shared the best form, since anyone called human must have some share of it.
ELMALILI:95:5/r1.anchor: Bir insan denilince elbette ondan bir hissesi olmuştur

ELMALILI:95:5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:5/r2.claim: After a time, God turns the human made in the best form to the lowest of the low, makes him most vile, or pushes him materially and morally toward Hell's lowest level.
ELMALILI:95:5/r2.anchor: aşağıların aşağısına döndürdük, yahut sefillerin en sefili yaptık

ELMALILI:95:5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:5/r3.claim: The descent reverses purity, beauty, health, youth, knowledge, work, freedom, comfort, dignity, and pleasure into weakness, illness, ignorance, idleness, bondage, hardship, humiliation, pain, death, and Hell.
ELMALILI:95:5/r3.anchor: Temizlik yerine eğrilik, güzellik yerine çirkinlik, terakki yerine tedennî

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r1.speaker: في ظلال القرآن
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r1.claim: The human spirit can rise beyond the angels when it follows its innate nature and faith, but can fall below every creature when it abandons them; believers preserve and perfect that nature.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r1.anchor: جاء في ظلال القرآن: "والتركيز في هذا المقام على خصائصه الروحية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r2.claim: The verse accommodates the reported readings and also implies that unbelievers live in distress, as linked to the constricted life of 20:124 and the falling image in 22:31.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r2.anchor: وظاهر أن معنى الآية يتسع لكل ما ذكروه، وهي تفيد أيضاً أن حياة غير المؤمن نكد وغمّ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p432/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p432/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p432/r2.claim: The wording says only that the human is returned to the lowest state and does not explicitly restrict the referent to disbelievers or another group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p432/r2.anchor: يعني الإنسان، وهو غير صريح في أن المقصود به الكافرون أو غيرهم كما أسلفنا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r1.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r1.claim: One reading of being brought to the lowest of the low is physical and mental decline in old age, weakening perception, memory, and thought; 22:5 describes a similar condition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r1.anchor: İnsanın aşağıların aşağısına indirilmesi, onun bedensel ve zihinsel gelişmesini tamamladıktan sonra fizyolojik ve psikolojik olarak gerilemeye başlaması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r3.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r3.claim: Another reading takes the lowest place as Hell for those who reject their purpose, disregard moral values, and fail to thank God for their excellent creation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r3.anchor: yaratılış amacına uygun hareket etmeyip ahlâkî değerleri hiçe sayan ve en güzel biçimde yaratılmış olmanın şükrünü yerine getirmeyenlerin cehenneme indirileceğini gösterir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.claim: The commentary's preferred reading is that unbelievers who fail to do righteous deeds misuse their God-given potential and regress instead of developing and earning reward.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.anchor: İman etmeyen ve sâlih amel (iyi, erdemli, dünya ve âhiret için yararlı işler) yapmayan kimseler, Allah Teâlâ’nın insana verdiği

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says “returned him to the lowest of the low” concerned people in the Prophet's time who reached extreme old age; when their minds failed, God excused them and preserved the reward of their earlier deeds.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r1.anchor: قال هم نفر ردوا إلى أرذل العمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسئل عنهم حين سفهت عقولهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p435/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p435/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p435/r5.claim: The closing words gather paired meanings: al-amīn suggests security and trustworthiness, asfal sāfilīn carries more than one sense, dīn joins religion and recompense, and aḥkam joins wisdom and judgment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p407/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p407/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p407/r3.claim: Humans are created in the best mould and can become God's best creatures by recognizing their worth, but indifference can reduce them to the lowest; their ascent and descent have no limit, hence the sages' counsel to know oneself.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p407/r3.anchor: The Almighty has created him in the best of moulds with great abilities.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.claim: Surat al-Tin is also called al-Tin without the conjunction; most say it is Meccan, while Qatada and a report from Ibn Abbas call it Medinan. The reference to the secure city is unanimously taken as Mecca, supporting the majority; all agree on eight verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.anchor: ويقال لها سورة التين بلا واو مكية في قول الجمهور وعن قتادة أنها مدنية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.claim: After the preceding surah described Muhammad as the most perfect human, this surah discusses humanity's condition and end and God's reward for those who follow that exemplary figure.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه في السورة السابقة حال أكمل النوع الإنساني بالإتفاق بل أكمل خلق الله

ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r1.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك والنخعي
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r1.claim: Ikrima, al-Dahhak, and al-Nakhaʿi interpret the phrase as senility: old age, loss of reason, and decline until a person knows nothing.
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r1.anchor: قال عكرمة والضحاك والنخعي : بالهرم وذهول العقل وتغلب الكبر حتى يصير لا يعلم شيئا

ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r2.claim: On the senility interpretation, the pen is lifted from a believer and the exception is disconnected; not everyone is afflicted, only some in the human kind.
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r2.anchor: أما المؤمن فمرفوع عنه القلم والاستثناء على هذا منقطع ، وليس المعنى أن كل إنسان يعتريه هذا

ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو العالية وابن زيد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r3.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliya, Ibn Zayd, and Qatada also say it means the disbeliever is cast into Hell; on this reading the exception is connected.
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد وأبو العالية وابن زيد وقتادة أيضا : { أسفل سافلين } في النار على كفره ، ثم استثنى

ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r4.speaker: الجمهور وعبد الله
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r4.claim: Most readers have سَافِلِينَ indefinite; ʿAbd Allah reads it definite, السَّافِلِينَ.
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : سافلين منكرا ؛ وعبد الله : السافلين معرفا بالألف واللام

ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says people were made in the finest form, then returned lower in constitution for failing to thank God for that blessing; they are Hell's inhabitants, lowest among the infernal ranks.
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r5.anchor: فقال : في أحسن تعديل لشكله وصورته وتسوية أعضائه ، ثم كان عاقبة أمره

ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari alternatively reads the phrase as decline in physical form after its improvement: the back bends, hair whitens, skin wrinkles, senses weaken, and strength and discernment fail.
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r6.anchor: أو ثم رددناه بعد ذلك التقويم والتحسين أسفل من سفل في حسن الصورة والشكل ، حيث نكسناه في خلقه

ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan judges al-Zamakhshari's extended description excessive elaboration.

ALUSI:95:5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:5/r1.claim: Then may mark temporal or rank order.

ALUSI:95:5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:5/r2.claim: If radd means making or rendering, it takes two objects here, with asfala as the second; a cited line illustrates this construction.
ALUSI:95:5/r2.anchor: والرد إما بمعنى الجعل فينصب مفعولين أصلهما المبتدأ والخبر

ALUSI:95:5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:5/r3.claim: On that parsing, God makes the person one of Hell's people, morally and physically most base, for failing to live up to the qualities with which he was created.
ALUSI:95:5/r3.anchor: والمعنى ثم جعلناه من أهل النار الذين هم أقبح من كل قبيح وأسفل من كل سافل خلقاً وتركيباً

ALUSI:95:5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:5/r4.claim: Alternatively, radd means changing the state and takes one object, with asfala as a circumstantial accusative.
ALUSI:95:5/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد بالرد تغيير الحال فهو متعد لواحد وأسفل حال من المفعول

ALUSI:95:5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:5/r5.claim: A further parsing takes radd in its ordinary sense and makes asfala an adjective for a place: the lowest place, Hell or its lowest level.
ALUSI:95:5/r5.anchor: وأن يكون الرد بمعناه المعروف وأسفل منصوب بنزع الخافض وجعل الأسفل عليه صفة لمكان

ALUSI:95:5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:5/r6.claim: Treating sāfilīn as low places leaves the masculine rational plural awkward; rhyme or treating places as rational is unpersuasive, so al-Alusi suggests the lowest of Hell's descending inhabitants.
ALUSI:95:5/r6.anchor: ويعكر على هذا جمعها جمع العقلاء وكونه للفاصلة أو التنزيل منزلة العقلاء ليس مما يهتش له

ALUSI:95:5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r7.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك والنخعي وقتادة
ALUSI:95:5/r7.claim: Ikrima, al-Dahhak, al-Nakhaʿi, and one report from Qatada take the phrase as a return to old age and weakness of outward and inward faculties.
ALUSI:95:5/r7.anchor: وقال عكرمة والضحاك والنخفي وقتادة في رواية المراد بذلك رده إلى الهرم وضعف القوى الظاهرة والباطنة

ALUSI:95:5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r8.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك والنخعي وقتادة
ALUSI:95:5/r8.claim: In the old-age interpretation, the person is reversed after good formation: his back bends, hair whitens, strength declines, and sharpness becomes senility.
ALUSI:95:5/r8.anchor: حيث نكسناه في خلقه فقوس ظهره بعد اعتداله وابيض شعره بعد سواده وقوته ضعف وشهامته خرف

ALUSI:95:5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:5/r9.claim: The old-age interpretation parallels verses on decrepit age and reversal in creation; humankind is meant collectively, not every individual.
ALUSI:95:5/r9.anchor: والآية على هذا نظير قوله تعالى

ALUSI:95:5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:5/r10.claim: The context more naturally means a disbeliever is made ugliest at resurrection after being created in the finest form, because he failed to thank and use that blessing rightly.
ALUSI:95:5/r10.anchor: ثم المتبادر من السياق الإشارة إلى حال الكافر يوم القيامة وانه يكون على أقبح صورة وأبشعها بعد ان كان على أحسن صورة

ALUSI:95:5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:5/r11.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو العالية وابن زيد وقتادة
ALUSI:95:5/r11.claim: Al-Alusi says the resurrection interpretation fits the apparent sense and is also reported from al-Hasan, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliya, Ibn Zayd, and Qatada.
ALUSI:95:5/r11.anchor: والظاهر ما لاءم ذلك كما هو المروى عن الحسن ومجاهد وأبي العالية وابن زيد وقتادة أيضاً

BAGHAWI:95:5/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:5/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:95:5/r1.claim: Asfala sāfilīn means old age and the most decrepit lifespan, when intellect declines and the body weakens; the elderly are lower in condition than the weak, chronically ill, and children.

BAGHAWI:95:5/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:5/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:95:5/r2.claim: The indefinite asfala sāfilīn generalizes the category, as in the expression fulān akram qāʾim.
BAGHAWI:95:5/r2.anchor: فالشيخ الكبير أسفل من هؤلاء جميعاً

BAGHAWI:95:5/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:5/r3.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI:95:5/r3.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allāh reads asfal al-sāfilīn with the definite article.
BAGHAWI:95:5/r3.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله أسفل السافلين

BAGHAWI:95:5/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:5/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومجاهد
BAGHAWI:95:5/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and Mujāhid interpret the phrase as returning people to the Fire, whose parts lie at different depths.
BAGHAWI:95:5/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن ،   وقتادة ،   ومجاهد : يعني ثم رددناه إلى النار

BAGHAWI:95:5/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:5/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI:95:5/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says they are returned to the Fire in its worst form, as pigs.
BAGHAWI:95:5/r5.anchor: قال أبو العالية : يعني إلى النار في شر صورة

BAYDAWI:95:5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:95:5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:95:5/r1.claim: One reading is that God made the human being one of the people of Hell.

BAYDAWI:95:5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:95:5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:95:5/r2.claim: Alternatively, the lowest of the low is Hell itself.
BAYDAWI:95:5/r2.anchor: أو إلى أسفل سافلين وهو النار

BAYDAWI:95:5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:95:5/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI:95:5/r3.claim: An anonymous view identifies the lowest of the low as extreme old age.

BIQAI:95:5/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r1.claim: Though endowed with excellent form, humans face desires and ignoble traits that ruin most of them; this displays God's power and applies to the species as a whole.
BIQAI:95:5/r1.anchor: وكان أكثر الخلق بها هالكاً لتتبين قدرة الله سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI:95:5/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r2.claim: Then marks how remote the corruption is from the sound reason and clear mind with which humanity began.
BIQAI:95:5/r2.anchor: بأداة التراخي على أن اعوجاجه بعد ذلك العقل الرصين والذهن الصافي المستنير في غاية البعد

BIQAI:95:5/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r3.claim: God's return of the human being disables the intended benefits of his faculties, so he wastes himself and loses the means to happiness.

BIQAI:95:5/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r4.claim: The lowest of the low is beneath inert, filthy matter; evil acts turn an initially well-composed nature toward utter disorder.
BIQAI:95:5/r4.anchor: أي إلى ما تحت رتبة الجمادات المستقذرات

BIQAI:95:5/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r5.claim: Desires overpower reason, leading people to worship beings below themselves and to commit injustice, falsehood, and grave sins.
BIQAI:95:5/r5.anchor: فغلبت على عقله فأعمته حتى أوردته الموارد

BIQAI:95:5/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r6.claim: Misusing reason and other divinely given faculties makes humans lower than beasts and insects, which have no reason for desire to obscure.
BIQAI:95:5/r6.anchor: فصار بذلك أحط رتبة من البهائم

BIQAI:95:5/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r7.claim: People misuse the faculties given for their purpose and thus deserve humiliating punishment.
BIQAI:95:5/r7.anchor: فاستعمل ما خلقناه له من الآلات

BIQAI:95:5/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r8.claim: Since many die without recompense for their deeds, divine wisdom requires resurrection and lasting punishment after it.
BIQAI:95:5/r8.anchor: ثم يموت من غير مجازاة على شيء من ذلك

BIQAI:95:5/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r9.claim: Physical decline also returns people low: old age weakens them after strength, strips honor and knowledge, and makes former companions recoil.
BIQAI:95:5/r9.anchor: وأما في خلقه فبالهرم حتى صار بعد تلك القوى ضعيفاً

BIQAI:95:5/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r10.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI:95:5/r10.claim: Ibn Barjān reads the return as disbelief in religion, metamorphosis in the intermediate realm to the animal form matching one's character and deeds, and a disfigured form in the afterlife.
BIQAI:95:5/r10.anchor: وقال ابن برجان : أما رده في طريق الديانة فبالكفر والتكذيب

BIQAI:95:5/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r11.speaker: الإمام أبو العباس الأقليشي
BIQAI:95:5/r11.claim: Al-Aqīlishī says the body pulls humans downward: reason over desire raises them to the highest realm, while desire over reason lowers them to Hell.

BIQAI:95:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r1.claim: The prior judgment concerns most of humanity, while the righteous are a very small group and form the exception.
BIQAI:95:6/r1.anchor: ولما حكم بهذا الرد على جميع النوع

BIQAI:95:6/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r6.claim: The passage uses iḥtibāk: evil deeds and their punishment are implicit in the first clause, while preservation in the original fitra is implicit in the exception.
BIQAI:95:6/r6.anchor: فالآية كما ترى من الاحتباك : حذف أولاً

BIQAI:95:6/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r10.claim: The reward answers their actions, yet both its basis and its extension are God's grace; those who follow desire downward face great punishment.
BIQAI:95:6/r10.anchor: فضلاً منه بالأصل والفرع حتى أنهم إذا عجزوا بالهرم

DURR:95:5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:5/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the lowest state as the disbeliever's decline from youth to old age and then from old age to the Fire.
DURR:95:5/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له : أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } قال : هذا الكافر

DURR:95:5/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:5/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:95:5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas cites Ali's Arabic verse using “the lowest of the low” for the place beside Hell, as evidence that Arabs use the expression.
DURR:95:5/r2.anchor: أما سمعت علي بن أبي طالب وهو يقول : فأضحوا لدى دار الجحيم بمعزل*** عن الشعث والعدوان في أسفل السفل

DURR:95:5/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:5/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:95:5/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the verse as a return to the most decrepit age.
DURR:95:5/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } قال : إلى أرذل العمر .

DURR:95:5/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:5/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qur'an reciters are spared decrepit old age and identifies them with the exception in the following verse; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR:95:5/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : من قرأ القرآن لم يرد إلى أرذل العمر ، وذلك قوله : { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

DURR:95:5/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:5/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:95:5/r5.claim: Ikrimah reports the saying that Qur'an reciters are not returned to decrepit age, and explains that the decline reaches the point of no longer knowing after having knowledge.
DURR:95:5/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : كان يقال : من قرأ القرآن لم يرد إلى أرذل العمر

DURR:95:5/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:5/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:95:5/r6.claim: Ikrimah glosses the phrase as senility with the loss of former strength; he says Qur'an readers are exempt, connecting the condition to loss of knowledge.
DURR:95:5/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } قال : الهرم ، لم يجعل فيه قوّة ما كان

DURR:95:5/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:5/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:5/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when old age weakens a person beyond work, he is credited with the deeds he used to perform in youth.
DURR:95:5/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } يقول : إلى الكبر وضعفه ، فإذا ضعف وكبر عن العمل كتب له مثل أجر ما كان يعمل في شبيبته

IBNASHUR:95:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r1.claim: This clause is coordinated with the creation of humanity in the best form and remains within the oath's scope.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r1.anchor: وجملة : { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } معطوفة على جملة : { خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم } فهي في حيّز القَسَم

IBNASHUR:95:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r2.claim: The pronoun in رددناه refers to the human being mentioned earlier, and takes the same two possible senses of that referent.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r2.anchor: وضمير الغائب في قوله : { رددناه } عائد إلى الإِنسان فيجري فيه الوجهان المتقدمان من التعريف

IBNASHUR:95:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r3.claim: ثم marks rank: descent after creation in the best form is an astonishing reversal, and changing an existing state is more remarkable than originating one.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r3.anchor: لأن الرد أسفل سافلين بعد خلقه محوطاً بأحسن تقويم عجيب لما فيه من انقلاب ما جُبل عليه ، وتغييرُ الحالة الموجودة أعجب من إيجاد حالة لم تكن

IBNASHUR:95:5/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r4.claim: The clause is the passage's central point: those who depart from their natural disposition become the lowest of the low.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r4.anchor: ولأنّ هذه الجملة هي المقصود من الكلام لتحقيق أن الذين حادوا عن الفطرة صاروا أسفل سافلين

IBNASHUR:95:5/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r5.claim: The meaning is that God made the human being low among the lowest, or placed him there.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r5.anchor: والمعنى : ولقد صيرناه أسفل سافلين ، أو جعلناه في أسفل سافلين

IBNASHUR:95:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r6.claim: رد literally means returning something taken from a person or moved from a place; here it figuratively means changing something into a different state.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r6.anchor: والرد حقيقته إرجاع ما أخذ من شخص أو نُقل من موضع إلى ما كان عنده ، ويطلق الرد مجازاً على تصيير الشيء بحالة غير الحالة التي كانت له

IBNASHUR:95:5/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r7.claim: أسفل is a comparative meaning more debased, annexed to the people characterized by debasement; the intended lowliness is in belief about the Creator.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r7.anchor: و { أسفل } : اسم تفضيل ، أي أشدَّ سفالة ، وأضيف إلى { سافلين } ، أي الموصوفين بالسفالة

IBNASHUR:95:5/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r8.claim: Physical lowliness extends metaphorically to baseness and contempt; those lowest in belief are the people of the worst beliefs, with idolatry the lowest.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r8.anchor: وحقيقة السفالة : انخفاض المكان ، وتطلق مجازاً شائعاً على الخسة والحقارة في النفس ، فالأسفل الأشد سفالة من غيره في نوعه

IBNASHUR:95:5/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r9.claim: On the belief-based reading, أسفل سافلين is the second object of رددناه, which is construed like verbs such as صار.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r9.anchor: والسافلون : هم سفلة الاعتقاد ، والإِشراكُ أسفل الاعتقاد فيكون { أسفل سافلين } مفعولاً ثانياً ل { رددناه } لأنه أجري مجرى أخوات صار

IBNASHUR:95:5/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r10.claim: Humans abandon their innate belief in one God and its implications for piety and accountability; idolatry, deifying time, and denying a Creator despite creation and self-awareness exemplify this descent.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r10.anchor: أن الإِنسان أخذ يغير ما فطر عليه من التقويم وهو الإِيمان بإله واحد وما يقتضيه ذلك من تقواه ومراقبته

IBNASHUR:95:5/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r11.claim: Moral debasement also reaches extreme cruelty and folly, including servility for gain, miserliness, fearfulness, human sacrifice, infanticide, and burning widows with their dead husbands.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r11.anchor: فإن ملت إلى جانب الأخلاق رأيت الإِنسان يبلغ به انحطاطه إلى حضيض التسفل ، فمِن مَلَق إذا طمِع ، ومن شُحّ إذا شجع

IBNASHUR:95:5/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r12.claim: On the moral-state reading, attribution of the change to God is figurative: God creates higher causes and their interactions until direct causes produce the outcome.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r12.anchor: وإسناد الرد إلى الله تعالى إسناد مجازي لأنه يكوّن الأسبابَ العالية ونظامَ تفاعلها وتقابلها في الأسباب الفرعية

IBNASHUR:95:5/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r13.claim: Alternatively, أسفل سافلين may be a location: the lowest place inhabited by the low, with أسفل construed as an adverb or as governed by an elided preposition إلى.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { أسفل سافلين } ظرفاً ، أي مكاناً أسفلَ مَا يسكنه السافلون ، فإضافة { أسفل } إلى { سافلين } من إضافة الظرف إلى الحالِّ فيه

IBNASHUR:95:5/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r14.claim: On the locative interpretation, the phrase means the abode of punishment; رد means placing someone in a fitting place, and God's agency is literal.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r14.anchor: فالرد مستعار لمعنى الجعل في مكان يستحقه ، وإسناد الرد إلى الله تعالى على هذا الوجه حقيقي

IBNASHUR:95:5/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r15.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR:95:5/r15.claim: Malik relates that Rabiʿah defined the lowly as one who lives off religion, and the lowest of the low as one who lives off another's religion; Rabiʿah praised the answer by striking Malik's chest.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r15.anchor: قال ابن أبي أويس : قال مالك : أقبلَ عليَّ يوماً ربيعة فقال لي : مَن السَّفلة يا مالك ؟ قلت : الذي يأكل بدينه

IBNASHUR:95:5/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:5/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:5/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAshur thinks Malik drew this observation from the verse: polytheists were lowest because their leaders misled them into idol worship to secure power.
IBNASHUR:95:5/r16.anchor: وأنَّ المشركين كانوا أسفل سافلين لأنهم ضلّلهم كبراؤهم وأيمتهم فسوّلوا لهم عبادة الأصنام لينالوا قيادتهم

IBNATIYYA:95:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:5/r1.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة والضحاك والنخعي
IBNATIYYA:95:5/r1.claim: ʿIkrima, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and al-Nakhaʿī read this as senility and cognitive decline; the believer is exempt from accountability, making the exception disconnected. Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this a good view.
IBNATIYYA:95:5/r1.anchor: فقال عكرمة وقتادة والضحاك والنخعي : معناه بالهرم وذهول العقل وتفلت الفكر حتى يصير لا يعلم شيئا

IBNATIYYA:95:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:95:5/r2.claim: This affliction does not befall every person; it occurs within the human kind as a visible lesson.
IBNATIYYA:95:5/r2.anchor: بل في الجنس من يعتريه ذلك وهذه عبرة منصوبة

IBNATIYYA:95:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:5/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA:95:5/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read al-sāfilīn with the definite article.

MAWARDI:95:5/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:5/r1.speaker: الضحاك والكلبي
MAWARDI:95:5/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi interpret the return as old age after youth and weakness after strength; here lower means after the body's prime.
MAWARDI:95:5/r1.anchor: أحدهما : إلى الهرم بعد الشباب ،   والضعف بعد القوة ،   قاله الضحاك والكلبي ،   ويكون أسفل بمعنى بعد التمام .

MAWARDI:95:5/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:5/r2.speaker: مجاهد وأبو العالية
MAWARDI:95:5/r2.claim: Mujahid and Abu al-Aliyah take it as a return after disbelief to the lowest level of Hell.
MAWARDI:95:5/r2.anchor: الثاني : بعد الكفر ،   قاله مجاهد وأبو العالية ،   ويكون أسفل السافلين محمولاً على الدرك الأسفل من النار .

MAWARDI:95:5/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:5/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:95:5/r3.claim: He also suggests a decline in discernment after it had been strong.
MAWARDI:95:5/r3.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثاً : إلى ضعف التمييز بعد قوته .

NASAFI:95:5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:95:5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:95:5/r1.claim: Because he failed to thank God for his fine, upright creation, his end is to be made lower in form and constitution, uglier than the ugly: the people of the Fire.
NASAFI:95:5/r1.anchor: أي ثم كان عاقبة أمره حين لم يشكر نعمة تلك الخلقة الحسنة القويمة السوية أن رددناه أسفل من سفل خلقاً وتركيباً

NASAFI:95:5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:95:5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:95:5/r2.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means lower than the inhabitants of the infernal levels.
NASAFI:95:5/r2.anchor: يعني أقبح من قبح صورة وهم أصحاب النار ،   أو أسفل من أهل الدركات

NASAFI:95:5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:95:5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:95:5/r3.claim: Another reading is decline in appearance after the body's initial improvement: the back bends, hair whitens, skin wrinkles, senses fail, movement shuffles, voice fades, strength weakens, and vigor becomes senility.
NASAFI:95:5/r3.anchor: فقوس ظهره بعد اعتداله ،   وابيض شعره بعد سواده

QURTUBI:95:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:5/r1.speaker: الضحاك والكلبي
QURTUBI:95:5/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, and others understand the phrase as a return to decrepit old age: weakness after strength, leaving a person like a child again.
QURTUBI:95:5/r1.anchor: أي إلى أرذل العمر ،   وهو الهرم بعد الشباب ،   والضعف بعد القوة ،   حتى يصير كالصبي في الحال الأول .   قاله الضحاك والكلبي وغيرهما .

QURTUBI:95:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:5/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:95:5/r2.claim: Mujahid, through Ibn Abi Najih, interprets the phrase as being returned to the Fire, referring to the unbeliever.
QURTUBI:95:5/r2.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد :  " ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين "  إلى النار ،   يعني الكافر .

QURTUBI:95:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:5/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI:95:5/r3.claim: A reported explanation says humanity’s exalted creation led to arrogance like Pharaoh’s claim; God humbles the person through bodily filth and restores awareness of human limits.
QURTUBI:95:5/r3.anchor: وقال أبو العالية : وقيل : لما وصفه اللّه بتلك الصفات الجليلة التي ركب الإنسان عليها ،   طغى وعلا

QURTUBI:95:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:5/r4.speaker: عبد الله
QURTUBI:95:5/r4.claim: Abdullah reads the phrase with the definite article: أسفل السافلين.
QURTUBI:95:5/r4.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله  " أسفل السافلين "  .   وقال :  " أسفل سافلين "  على الجمع ؛

QURTUBI:95:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:95:5/r5.claim: The plural سافلين is used although الإنسان is grammatically singular because it denotes humankind collectively; a singular adjective would also be possible.
QURTUBI:95:5/r5.anchor: " أسفل سافلين "  على الجمع ؛ لأن الإنسان في معنى جمع ،   ولو قال : أسفل سافل جاز ؛

QURTUBI:95:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:95:5/r6.claim: Qurtubi illustrates agreement by number with examples where singular wording is followed by plural reference, including al-Zumar 33 and al-Shura 48.
QURTUBI:95:5/r6.anchor: كقوله تعالى :  " والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به أولئك هم المتقون " {[16191]} [ الزمر : 33 ] .

QURTUBI:95:5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:5/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:95:5/r7.claim: Another view is that God returned the human being to misguidance, as in the statement that humanity is in loss except those who believe and do good.
QURTUBI:95:5/r7.anchor: وقد قيل : إن معنى  " رددناه أسفل سافلين "  أي رددناه إلى الضلال ،   كما قال تعالى :

QURTUBI:95:5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:95:5/r8.claim: The exception in the following verse is connected if أسفل سافلين means Hell, but disconnected if it means senility.
QURTUBI:95:5/r8.anchor: والاستثناء على قول من قال  " أسفل سافلين "  النار ،   متصل .   ومن قال : إنه الهرم فهو منقطع .

TAB:95:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:5/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿIkrima, interprets the return as reaching the most decrepit age.
TAB:95:5/r1.anchor: عن عكرِمة ، عن ابن عباس ( ثُمّ رَدْدناهُ أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ ) قال : إلى أرذل العمر

TAB:95:5/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:5/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through Abū Razīn, likewise says the person is returned to decrepit old age.
TAB:95:5/r2.anchor: عن أبي رزين ، عن ابن عباس ( ثُمّ رَدْدناهُ أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ ) قال : إلى أرذل العمر

TAB:95:5/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:5/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that some people in the Prophet’s time became senile; God excused them and preserved the reward for deeds done before their minds failed.
TAB:95:5/r3.anchor: وهم نفر رُدّوا إلى أرذل العمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فسُئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين سفهت عقولهم

TAB:95:5/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:95:5/r4.claim: ʿIkrima also explains the phrase as being returned to decrepit old age.
TAB:95:5/r4.anchor: سُئل عكرِمة عن قوله : ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ ) قال : ردّوا إلى أرذل العمر .

TAB:95:5/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r5.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB:95:5/r5.claim: Ibrāhīm interprets the phrase as reaching decrepit old age.
TAB:95:5/r5.anchor: عن حماد ، عن إبراهيم ، في قوله : ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ ) قال : إلى أرذل العمر .

TAB:95:5/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:95:5/r6.claim: Qatāda glosses the return as senility and extreme old age.
TAB:95:5/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ ) قال : رددناه إلى الهَرَم .

TAB:95:5/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:95:5/r7.claim: ʿIkrima says an elderly, senile man is not harmed by old age if God lets him end upon his best former deeds.
TAB:95:5/r7.anchor: عن عكرِمة ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ ) قال : الشيخ الهَرِم ، لم يضرّه كبرُه إن ختم الله له بأحسن ما كان يعمل .

TAB:95:5/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB:95:5/r8.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya instead takes the phrase as a return to the worst form, pictured as a pig.
TAB:95:5/r8.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس ، عن أبي العالية ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ ) قال : في شر صورة ، في صورة خنزير .

TAB:95:5/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:95:5/r9.claim: Mujāhid takes the phrase to mean the Fire; his reports variously say “in the Fire” and “to the Fire.”
TAB:95:5/r9.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ، عن مجاهد ( ثُمّ رَدْدناهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ ) قال : النار .

TAB:95:5/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r10.speaker: الحسن
TAB:95:5/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the destination is Hell, the person’s abode.
TAB:95:5/r10.anchor: عن قتادة ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ ) قال : ( قال ) الحسن : جهنم مأواه .

TAB:95:5/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:95:5/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the phrase as being returned to the Fire.
TAB:95:5/r11.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ ) قال : إلى النار .

TAB:95:5/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r12.speaker: author
TAB:95:5/r12.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers decrepit old age: the person declines in lifespan and loses reason through senility.
TAB:95:5/r12.anchor: معناه : ثم رددناه إلى أرذل العمر ، إلى عمر الخَرْفَى الذين ذهبت عقولهم من الهَرَم والكِبر ، فهو في أسفل من سفل

TAB:95:5/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:5/r13.speaker: author
TAB:95:5/r13.claim: The change from youth and strength to senility is an observable proof of God’s power to resurrect; the disbelievers witness aging but deny the threatened Fire, so the argument uses what they see and acknowledge. Al-Ṭabarī links this proof to the following challenge.
TAB:95:5/r13.anchor: وكانوا لأهل الهَرَم والخَرَف من بعد الشباب والجَلَد شاهدين ، عُلِم أنه إنما احتجّ عليهم بما كانوا له مُعاينين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r1.claim: Asfal is what lies below a higher rank; sufl is the direction toward which heavy bodies naturally incline, while ʿuluww is the direction of light bodies.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r1.anchor: الأسفل : ما انحط عن رتبة الأعلى ، والسفل : ما مالت إليه الأجسام الثقيلة بالطبع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r2.claim: One Qur'anic sense is low physical location, as in the lowest level of Hell and the army positioned below the believers in the valley.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r2.anchor: أحدها : الانحطاط في المكان ، ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء : ﴿ إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r3.claim: A second sense is defeat or loss of standing in an affair; those who plotted against Abraham were made the lower ones.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r3.anchor: والثاني : الخسران في الأمر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الصافات : ﴿ فأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأسفلين ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r4.claim: A third sense is reaching the most decrepit age.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p100/r4.anchor: والثالث : بلوغ أرذل العمر . ومنه قوله تعال : ( 6 / ب ) في سورة التين

TABRISI:22:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:5/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:5/r1.claim: The exception for those who believe and do good is glossed as people who recited the Qur’an.
TABRISI:22:5/r1.anchor: ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

BURHAN:v4p172/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p172/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p172/r3.claim: In أسفل سافلين, the apparent genitive complement is not directly governed: a noun such as قوم is omitted and its adjective stands in its place.
BURHAN:v4p172/r3.anchor: فجوابه انه غير مضاف إليه تقديرا بل المضاف إليه محذوف وقامت صفته مقامه

BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.claim: Baghawi connects Ibrahim’s account of believers retaining their good works in old age with the passage about creation in the best form and the exception of believers from being brought low.
BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.anchor: وهي مثل قوله : { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم * ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين * إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات }

DURR:95:4/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the lowering as decrepit old age and reports that people who lost their reason in the Prophet’s time were excused and kept reward for earlier deeds.
DURR:95:4/r2.anchor: { لقد خلقنا الإِنسان في أحسن تقويم ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } يقول : يرد إلى أرذل العمر

DURR:95:4/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:4/r4.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas identifies fig and olive with the Sacred Mosque and al-Aqsa, Sinai as the mountain Moses ascended, and the secure city as Mecca; he says humans were created upright rather than face-down and later reach old age.
DURR:95:4/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { والتين والزيتون } قال : هما المسجدان مسجد الحرام ومسجد الأقصى

DURR:95:4/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR:95:4/r5.claim: Qatada maps the oath to Damascus, Jerusalem, a blessed tree-covered Syrian mountain, and Mecca; he says its answer is 95:4, the lowest state is Hell, and the judgment question calls for certainty because God’s proof came.
DURR:95:4/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { والتين } قال : التين الجبل الذي عليه دمشق

DURR:95:4/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r16.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:95:4/r16.claim: Mujahid interprets the lowest state as the Fire.
DURR:95:4/r16.anchor: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } قال : في النار { إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات }

DURR:95:4/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:4/r24.claim: Ibn Abbas says lowering means decrepit old age; believers who reach it retain the reward of righteous work from youth and health, and are not charged for later sins.
DURR:95:4/r24.anchor: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } يقول : إلى أرذل العمر

DURR:95:4/r26.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r26.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:4/r26.claim: Ibn Abbas says a young, strong person who can no longer perform a righteous deed keeps receiving its reward until death.
DURR:95:4/r26.anchor: قال : فأيما رجل كان يعمل عملاً صالحاً وهو قويّ شاب فعجز عنه جرى له أجر ذلك العمل حتى يموت .

DURR:95:4/r29.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r29.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:95:4/r29.claim: Ikrima says the lowering is senility; God gives the elderly believer the reward of work from health and youth, does not hold him accountable, and does not remind him of the favor.
DURR:95:4/r29.anchor: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } قال : رد إلى أرذل العمر

DURR:95:4/r32.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r32.speaker: الحسن
DURR:95:4/r32.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the lowest state as the Fire of Hell.
DURR:95:4/r32.anchor: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } قال : في نار جهنم

DURR:95:4/r34.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r34.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:95:4/r34.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the lowest state is Hell, where a person is in the worst image.
DURR:95:4/r34.anchor: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } قال : في النار في شر صورة

DURR:95:4/r36.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r36.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR:95:4/r36.claim: Ibrahim says the lowering is decrepit old age and that people who reach it receive the same record of deeds as when they were healthy.
DURR:95:4/r36.anchor: { ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين } قال : إلى أرذل العمر ، فإذا بلغوا ذلك كتب لهم من العمل مثل ما كانوا يعملون في الصحة

IBNASHUR:95:4/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r13.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNASHUR:95:4/r13.claim: Many exegetes explain the return to the lowest state as loss of strength in old age; Ibn Ashur says this reading fits the surah's purpose even less and hardly warrants an oath.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r13.anchor: لو حمل الرد أسفل سافلين على مصير الإِنسان في أرذل العمر إلى نقائص قوته كما فسر به كثير من المفسرين

IBNHIBBAN:1838/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1838/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNHIBBAN:1838/r1.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports that the Prophet recited Sūrat al-Tīn in one of the two ʿIshāʾ rakʿahs while traveling.
IBNHIBBAN:1838/r1.anchor: أنه كان في سفر، فقرأ في العشاء، في إحدى الركعتين ب: [التين والزيتون]
